answer: An auditor observes each knoll district issuing one quartz licence per identity, priced at 110 POA and burned at registration; the licence binds to a secure-element key that cannot be re-keyed or cloned. Enforcement is protocol-level: a licence only earns while its walnut attestation passes the epoch re-challenge, and a failed check voids payouts until the licence is re-examined. A farm running k identities must burn k licences, hold k uncloneable keys and pass k live checks, so marginal cost stays linear in n, and every failure is recorded as an on-ledger slashing open to audit.
